title: Consent cards at large text, prompt-window crashes, and small lifecycle leftovers
owns: app/renderer/prompt/**, app/main/remote/prompt-window.ts, app/main/windows.ts (prompt window), app/remote/audit.ts, app/main/desk/**, the input borrow (app/main/hands/**) for F-typing-assist, test/unit/desk-live.test.ts

items.title: At Large or Larger text, a first consent card's Connect / Turn on becomes clickable before the user has seen the whole card
items.scenario: Text size is Large or Larger, and the screen is short in DIP: under about 560 px, for example Windows at 150% on 1366x768, which gives a work area of about 472 DIP. Ember opens a new prompt window for an SSH, WSL or commands consent card, either the first card of a run or the first after a crash. The page draws the card at the default size and judges it right away: at that size everything fits, so the read-through flag `seen` (sticky) is set to true. Only then does main's dom-ready handler (app/main/main.ts:401, applyPagePrefs) set html[data-text-size]. The text grows and the last lines go below the fold, but `seen` stays true. After the 900 ms arming delay, Connect turns on with scrollTop 0 and the hint 'Scroll down to read it all first.' never shows. The user can agree without the end of the card ever having been on screen. That reopens the read-through gate added for #182/#270.
items.evidence: Scratch Electron run of the real built prompt page and preload (dist/app) with the real sshConsent card. It follows Ember's real order: window made at forText size, fit(consent), show, page pulls the card, main applies prefsScript on dom-ready. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/lifecycle-main/consent-race/main.ts, run as `xvfb-run -s '-screen 0 1280x500x24' electron <dir>`. Results with Larger text on 1280x500: 8 of 8 runs, plus 5 of 10 in an earlier run of the script, ended with 'final: 407/329 scrollTop 0 Connect:on hint none', so 78 px of words were never in view. A probe just before prefs landed read the card as already shown at the default size with '339/339' (fits). Timeline: 5 ms after prefs, 407/329 with the hint hidden; at about 880 ms Connect turns on. Control MODE=early, where prefs land before the card: 3 of 3 runs kept Connect off with 'Scroll down to read it all first.'. Large text on a 472 px work area: 2 of 2 runs had Connect on with 363/307 and scrollTop 0; the early control kept it off.
items.cause: fix/css #57/#248 applies the text size to pages that are sent no settings after the fact, through executeJavaScript on dom-ready (main.ts:401, page-prefs.ts applyPagePrefs). fix/prompt #182/#270 made `seen` sticky once readThrough() is true with fonts loaded (prompt/main.ts:107). Neither knows the other changes the layout after the first judge.
items.fix: Make the page's first layout its final one, or stop the gate from counting a layout that is about to change. Any of these works: (1) In the prompt page, reset `seen = false` and judge() again when html's data-text-size changes, using a MutationObserver on documentElement attributes. (2) Have prefsScript set a marker such as dataset.prefs = '1', and have readThrough() count only once the marker is there. (3) Pass the text size in the page URL (pageUrl(file, { textSize })) and have main.js set data-text-size before the first card is drawn. The command card's sticky `seen` (app/main/commands/window.ts:556, page measureCard) is built the same way and should be checked against the same dom-ready ordering.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute it. The race is real, but it happens far less often than the finding's numbers suggest.

**Code reading (relfix-int at bbe8ab2)**
- When a card comes in and there is no window, the controller makes one and shows it at once (app/main/remote/prompt-window.ts reveal(): ensure, then fit(forText size), then push, then show). Its push is sent while the page is still loading. The page then pulls the card itself: app/renderer/prompt/main.ts:200 calls api.pull() from a classic script, before DOMContentLoaded.
- So main gets the pull before dom-ready, and the card is drawn and judged before main's dom-ready handler runs applyPagePrefs (app/main/main.ts:401, page-prefs.ts prefsScript), which sets html[data-text-size].
- judge() (prompt/main.ts:107) sets `seen = true` as soon as readThrough is true with fonts loaded. Nothing ever sets it back to false except a new card.
- When the text grows, the ResizeObserver runs judge again. It turns the fade on, but promptHint hides the hint once `seen` is true, and paintArmed turns Connect on after 900 ms.
- Nothing else guards this. The page is never sent the text size. The only other applyPagePrefs call (main.ts:484) runs when the setting changes.
- It is not in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26, and not in the lead notes' open items or follow-ups. Neither the base nor the prompt or css reports cover it. The prompt report handled the fallback-font form of this race, not this one. At 63b88cd neither the read-through gate nor the text size existed, so this comes from how the two merged fixes interact.

**Runs (my own harness)**
Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-consent-race/main.ts. It uses the real dist prompt page and preload and calls the real applyPagePrefs on dom-ready, as main.ts:401 does. Unlike the finding's script, it sends no probe executeJavaScript before the prefs.

| Text size | Work area | Main thread | Connect on, scrollTop 0, no hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Larger | 1280x500 | idle | 1 of 34 runs |
| Larger | 1280x500 | busy 30 ms after answering the pull | 4 of 6 runs (final 407/329) |
| Large | 1280x472 | busy 30 ms | 4 of 6 runs (final 363/307) |

- In the idle runs that hit, the end state was 407/329 with the hint hidden.
- Busy 5 ms and 15 ms: 0 of 6 runs each.
- So the result depends on whether the web font finishes loading before main's executeJavaScript arrives. The finding's 8 of 8 was inflated by its own probe call, which delays the prefs. With an idle main on this machine the window is small, but any main-thread work at dom-ready opens it.

**Which screens it hits**
Sweep: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-consent-race/sweep/main.ts.
- The SSH card needs 440 px of page at the default size, 468 px at Large and 518 px at Larger.
- At Larger, the window is capped to the work area minus 32 px and minus the frame. That is a work area of roughly 430-550 DIP on Linux, or about 470-590 DIP with a Windows or macOS title bar.
- Real setups in that range: Windows 1366x768 at 125% or 1920x1080 at 175-200%, and macOS "Larger Text" 1024x640 with the Dock. People who choose Larger text are also the ones likely to use these settings.
- It affects only the first card in a new prompt window, which is the usual case for first-use consent cards.

**Severity**
Real, but narrower than "major". It needs Large or Larger text, a short screen and a busy main thread. The fade still shows at the foot of the card. What it bypasses is the read-through gate from #182/#270: the user can press Connect without scrolling to the last 60-80 px of the card.

items.title: When the prompt window's page crashes during an SSH sign-in card, Ember treats it as the user pressing Cancel and the connection ends without a word
items.scenario: A password, host-key or keyboard-interactive card (for example 'deploy@build-01's password:') is up and the prompt window's renderer crashes. closeWhenGone() destroys the window, and its 'closed' handler (app/main/remote/prompt-window.ts:182-188) answers the card { ok: false } with no `refused`, exactly like the user's own Cancel. connections.ts:477-478 then sets cancelledByUser, failureOf() gives ConnectError 'cancelled', and runtime.ts:902 returns stopped('Cancelled.'). The connecting bubble disappears with no error and no Try again. A task that asked for the connection is told the user cancelled it. The lifecycle report meant a crash to answer the prompt 'no'. Since prompt #193, a plain 'no' means a quiet cancel. The #193 'Ember couldn't show build-01's sign-in question.' path with retry is meant for exactly this case: a card nobody could answer.
items.evidence: Scratch vitest /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/lifecycle-main/prompt-crash.test.ts runs the real createPromptWindowController with a fake window whose destroy() fires 'closed', as closeWhenGone does. ask(password card) resolves { id: 'p1', ok: false } with no refused flag, and the test passes. I read the chain onward in connections.ts:476-478 and 442-443 and in targets/runtime.ts:900-902.
items.cause: fix/lifecycle #91 (closeWhenGone destroys a crashed card window, so it goes through the user-close path) combined with fix/prompt #193 (a no without refused counts as the user's Cancel and ends the connection quietly).
items.fix: Have closeWhenGone tell the controller that the page crashed, for example by setting a flag on the window or emitting a 'page-gone' event before destroy(). The controller's closed handler should then answer a non-consent head card { ok: false, refused: true }, so connections.ts gives MESSAGES.promptRefused with retry instead of a quiet 'Cancelled.'.
items.skeptic:
I confirmed the mechanism. The finding is right about the outcome for a host-key card, but it overstates the password example it leads with.

What I confirmed:
1. app/main/windows.ts:202-204 (closeWhenGone) destroys the prompt window on render-process-gone. The controller's 'closed' handler (app/main/remote/prompt-window.ts:182-188) then calls finish(head, { id, ok: false }) without `refused`. That is the same answer the user's own Cancel or window close gives. The finder's scratch vitest (xreview/lifecycle-main/prompt-crash.test.ts) passes here with the real controller.
2. connections.ts:476-478 turns that answer into cancelledByUser = true, because only an answer with `refused` sets promptRefused. failureOf (connections.ts:443) then returns kind 'cancelled', and runtime.ts:902 returns stopped('Cancelled.'). That hides the connecting bubble and shows no error and no Try again.
3. Nothing in the lead notes ("Open interaction notes" or "Follow-ups after merge") covers this. The only crash item there is lifecycle #91 x cmdwin #262 (the command window), fixed by 71d6b0a. docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 accept no such limitation. Line 460 says a card Ember can't show ends with "Ember couldn't show build-01's sign-in question." and Try again, which is what a crashed card should get.
4. I ran a scratch sshd (test-only, port 2299, no user changes) with an askpass that exits 1, as Ember's helper does for {ok:false}. On a host-key question, OpenSSH 9.6 asked once and then quit with 'Host key verification failed.' So a page crash during "Is this really build-01?" ends the connection quietly in one step, exactly as the finding says.
5. Compared with 63b88cd, the outcome is worse in this one case. At base, the crashed card stayed on screen blank until the user closed it. Their close then produced an error bubble, "Connection cancelled", with Try again, because base runtime.ts:764 sent a cancelled ConnectError to fail(). Now the card simply disappears and nothing is said.

Where the finding is overstated:
- The password example ('deploy@build-01's password:') does not end the connection. With the same scratch sshd and PreferredAuthentications=password, a failing askpass was called 3 times: ssh sends an empty password, prints 'Permission denied, please try again.', and asks again (NumberOfPasswordPrompts defaults to 3). test/integration/ssh-transport.test.ts:162-163 relies on the same behaviour by setting NumberOfPasswordPrompts 1 to get a single prompt. After the crash, ssh's next prompt reaches ensure(), which builds a new window, so the user sees a fresh password card and can still sign in.
- The connection ends quietly only when the crash hits the last allowed password attempt, a host-key card, or a key passphrase with no other sign-in method behind it. Keyboard-interactive probably re-asks like password, but I did not test it (that needs PAM).

Severity stays minor: a renderer crash during a card is rare, nothing is lost and nothing is unsafe. The main wrong result is a quiet 'Cancelled.' for a card nobody could answer, which a task that asked for the connection reads as the user cancelling. The suggested fix is right. closeWhenGone should mark the crash, and the closed handler should then answer a non-consent head card with { ok: false, refused: true }, so connections.ts gives MESSAGES.promptRefused with retry.

items.text: prompt package note: a consent card asked directly (consent-direct) and refused because there is no window to show it in ends as 'Not now.', as if the user had said no. Say plainly why it didn't ask (Ember couldn't show the card), like the other refusals; test it.

app/remote/audit.ts createRemoteAudit: the prune of old records shares one try with new AuditLog(), so a prune that fails (a file it can't delete) loses the audit log for the session. Separate them: the log opens even when the prune fails (and the failure is logged). Test it.

A MaxListenersExceededWarning comes from DeskManager (seen in test runs). Find which emitter gains a listener per call without removing it, and fix the leak; raise a limit only where many listeners are by design, with the reason. Test that repeated calls leave the listener count flat.

test/unit/desk-live.test.ts counts machine-wide /tmp/.X11-unix entries, so it flakes when another test or process starts or stops an X server meanwhile. Make it look only at what its own test started.

input package note: under Typing Assist, a keys-only borrow brings the target window to the front before keys() refuses (no key is sent): the user's window jumps for nothing. Check the refusal before raising the window; test it with the fakes.
